utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today, we are Tuesday, the 23rd of September, 2008. I would like to greet the representatives of the Prosecution, Mr. Mundis, Mrs. Dahl, as well as Mr. Seselj and the Registrar, the usher, and all the people assisting us. The Trial Chamber has decided to sit today in order to address the various housekeeping matters that resulted from the stay of the proceedings over a number of weeks. Therefore, it is important to put this trial back on track, which was interrupted. As everybody knows, the Prosecutor had asked for a stay of the proceedings until such a time that the Trial Chamber decide on the motion of the Prosecution aimed at assigning a counsel for the accused. The Prosecutor, even as the Trial Chamber had decided to continue with the proceedings, the Prosecution then turned to the Trial Chamber and asked it to stay the proceedings until such a time the Appeals Chamber hand down a decision on the adjournment. As you know, the Appeals Chamber has recently handed down its decision, dismissing the arguments filed by the Prosecution. Under these conditions, we have instantly handed down a decision and asked the Prosecution to disclose to us the list of upcoming witnesses over the next few weeks, and we felt that it was important, before hearing our first witness, to review a number of housekeeping matters that are likely to be raised during the hearing that merit our attention. Today, since we will hear our first witness tomorrow, we can then address his testimony without having to deal with administrative matters, which could be time-consuming. Mr. Seselj, as you know, we have not seen each other for a number of weeks now. A lot of things have happened in the meantime. I assume that you have a number of topics you wish to address. Then I will give the floor back to the Prosecution, whom I assume also has a number of issues to raise. Mr. Seselj, I shall give you the floor now. What kind of issues would you like to address which are, of course, of interest to you and of interest to these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have a large number of questions to deal with, and I want these questions to be looked at one by one. The first question would be the problem related to my legal advisers. It was first of all caused by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, other microphones are on. Could they please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the trial started, my legal advisers visited me about once a month, and the Registry covered their travel expenses. Almost a month ago, I scheduled a visit by my legal advisers for the 25th and 26th of September, that is to say, Thursday and Friday this week, as if I had anticipated that we would have to restart this trial finally. It just so happened, although I did not have any such information available. This time the Registry refused to cover the travel expenses of my legal advisers, and they did not explicitly state whether this visit would be made possible or not, although the prison administration had provided me with a schedule of their visit very regularly. The Registry sent some letters to me and to the legal advisers. First of all, in these letters, the Registry criticises the legal advisers because of some public statements they made. For instance, Slavko Jerkovic, because he stated that The Hague Tribunal was trying to kill me, and that is my personal thesis as well, as well as of my legal advisers, because if you impose counsel on me, that equals attempted murder. Perhaps you don't see it that way, but that is exactly the way I see it, my legal advisers, and the entire Serbian public. Taking away my right to self-defence means liquidation. Even if that was not true, why could my legal adviser not state something like that? Who is there to stop him from doing that? Who is there to forbid him from doing that? The Registry? No way. The Registry invokes the code of defence counsel acting before this Tribunal. My legal advisers are not Defence counsel. It is not their task to guard the reputation of this Tribunal, because both I and my legal advisers believe that this Tribunal has no reputation whatsoever, moral or professional. I'm not saying this Trial Chamber; I'm saying the Tribunal as a whole. It doesn't have professional or moral authority or reputation, and that is my standpoint from Day 1. So I can only have as my legal adviser someone who follows me in that belief, not somebody who is going to oppose me in court and say, "This is a great court, and you, as my client, is disreputable." Not everybody has to enjoy a proper reputation here, both the Court and I. Somebody has to be in disrepute. Now what they hold against me is a statement made to the effect that the Prosecution is prepared to do anything just in order not to lose this trial, even to attempt murder by injecting air into veins and so on and so forth. Then Zoran Krasic is being criticised for having stated in public that Prosecution witnesses are liars, but that's what practically the entire Serbian public believes. Everything was heard in public session, and what was in closed session was even more drastic than what we heard in public session, and that truly corroborated what I just said now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. We will get back to this. Do not address the issue of those witnesses that are lying. If you like, I will address this a little later. For the time being, please only address the issues raised by your associates since this letter was sent by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just quoted what is contained in the letter of the Registrar. If you insist, I won't go on quoting it any longer. See, I'm very constructive. You tell me not to do that, and I don't do it. And I'm even obedient. This doesn't really suit me, but even I have turned into an obedient person now. So there you go. The Registry is trying to disqualify my legal advisers through political arguments. I don't allow that. I don't allow the Registry to lecture my legal advisers as to how they're going to behave in the Serbian public, because in addition to being my legal advisers, they are politicians in Serbia. They are public figures in Serbia. They have a standpoint of their own, which is in accordance with that held by the public opinion in Serbia. There is also some criticism levelled against Aleksandar Vucic here. In the meantime, I have dismissed him because I no longer trust him, so he's no longer my legal adviser; and there's no need to have a debate on that. What I'm asking you to do is to protect my legal adviser, and if the Registry did not resolve the question of financing my Defence, although you had instructed them to do so, let them not bring into question even the minimum that was resolved practically in 2000. Make it possible for my legal advisers to come here on Thursday and Friday, to come here to court, and then on Thursday and Friday they can come and visit me at the Detention Unit, as they've been visiting me until now. A second matter. Instead of Aleksandar Vucic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Please, I shall address the issue right away, and then you can continue. The Trial Chamber was advised of this, and I was advised of this yesterday, as you see, quite recently. I was told the Registrar had, in fact, sent a letter to your legal advisers. I discovered that they could not come, since they had not received a reply. Mrs. Raguz was not concerned by this letter, and admittedly Mr. Krasic and Mr. Vucic -- Mr. Vucic's case is now settled, and the third lawyer was asked to provide explanation on a confidentiality agreement. You know as well as I do that when the Registry has vetted your legal advisers, he asked them to sign a paper entitled "Confidentiality Agreement." This is something I've noticed many a time, since I'm informed in realtime of all the articles or interviews given by your legal advisers. The problem rests on what follows. Your legal advisers are members of Parliament that were elected on the basis of a political platform, and as such, as members of Parliament, they are entitled to take the floor. Nothing can go against that right, which is theirs, as they've been elected. They have an absolute right. However, they are entitled to give their opinion and they're entitled to state that this Tribunal is illegal. This is not a scoop, since this is something you have already mentioned. To say it once or twice, that's all very well, but to repeat it over and over again, I don't see that that is very useful. Sometimes, on looking at their speeches, of course we only have a translation of interviews or articles. Sometimes there may be a few mistakes in these. You have noticed that Mr. Jerkovic said that this Tribunal wanted to murder you. First of all, this is something that you know as well as I do, nobody wishes to murder you, and the Judges certainly do not wish to murder you. First of all, Mr. Jerkovic is anticipating a decision which has not been handed down yet, so why does he say this when he doesn't even know what kind of decision will be handed down? Let him wait for the decision to be handed down either to applaud it or to criticise it. But to anticipate this, he says that you're going to be murdered, when he doesn't even know what is going to be decided, and that is not the way things should be. It is not normal that somebody in his capacity should state, in public, that the Tribunal would want to murder someone, which would be a crime. Of course, it is important to pick up on his own words. Maybe he was being witty, maybe he was using metaphors, maybe that was the case. Mr. Krasic on several occasions, has also spoken in a way which I found rather surprising. It is very difficult for somebody like Mr. Krasic or Jerkovic to know and to establish a difference when they take the floor as members of Parliament or as legal advisers. It's difficult to know the difference. The Registrar is also in charge of the legal advisers, from a financial standpoint. The Registrar has done his work and has asked for these legal advisers to provide him with some information. If they breach the confidentiality agreement, then the Registrar is entitled to seize the Chamber and submit the problem to the Chamber. So let's wait and see what your associates have to say to this and how they will respond to the Registrar. I don't know. Your associates are there to help you. They're not there to harm you, and if, through their ill-advised statements, they confuse all and everyone, this is not the way things should be. They have attended the hearing many times, and I was sometimes tempted to talk to them, but I had rather we spend our time hearing the witness. Therefore, I did not speak to them directly, and I did not want to make them feel uncomfortable, since they have a political mandate and it's not for me to interfere with that in any way. So I didn't say anything. But as they're making statements and speeches all the time, we have reason to wonder whether they haven't overstepped their mark. The Registrar is asking them for explanations. It so happens that you had planned for them to come on the 25th and 26th of September. This is something I knew nothing about, since the Trial Chamber is not involved with that. It's unfortunate, perhaps, since it happens at that time. That is all I can say. We are waiting for them to answer the Registry's paper, and then the Trial Chamber will see what it should do. Sometimes we come across situations where the Trial Chamber needs to state that your legal advisers have overstepped their mark. Then, of course, we look into the matter and see whether they still have a mandate to assist you, because your legal advisers are there to help you and not to adversely affect your case. So we are waiting for the response of your associates. The Trial Chamber has been advised of the existence of this letter yesterday, which is something you confirmed this morning, so this is a very recent occurrence. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my legal advisers received this letter from the Registry on the 18th of September. What is stated in the letter is that the deadline for their response was the 19th of September. They did respond on the 19th of September, and they faxed their reply to the Registry. The Registry has received their reply, and the Registry does not have the right, before the Trial Chamber rules on this, to prevent their visit from taking place in advance or not to pay their travel expenses. It is my deep belief that the Registry cannot do that, but they are to go it, because the Registry is not an independent judiciary institution, it is an institution of court administration. It is governed by the principles of administrative law, not by principles governing the judiciary, and they cannot enter into procedural matters in this way. I think they cannot. If they did that in some other trials, then it is only even worse for the Tribunal. As for the other questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this particular matter is concerned, the Trial Chamber will meet after this hearing. We will deliberate on the matter, look into the responses they have provided. I know nothing about this at this stage. It's on the transcript, and we shall deliberate on this later. The second issue, which is connected to the first?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I informed the Registry in writing that I have appointed Boris Aleksic as my new legal adviser, and I request that he be allowed to visit on Thursday and Friday and to visit the courtroom, that he be accorded the same treatment as all other legal advisers. The Registry has not informed me of their view with regard to this matter yet. Tomorrow, all three legal advisers and the case manager are setting out on their journey. They'll be in The Hague. Now, what will be done in connection with their trip and whether it will all be in vain, that's a different matter altogether. It was for me to present this problem for you here in detail. And, thirdly, with regard to the first question, at the end of the letter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Mr. Boris Aleksic, which I do not know, who is he? Is he a legal adviser, a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He has a degree in law. He is a member of Parliament of the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, and for quite a while now he has a member of the professional team for assisting my Defence. So as for his qualities, as a highly-educated legal professional, I truly trust him, and that is why I have given him this trust. That is why he's a member of my team. And for quite a while now, you've been seeing his name on the front page or the cover page of my legal submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems, and I'd like to thank my colleague for having drawn my attention on this issue, the Registrar is concerned by the following: Since you are in contact with your legal advisers, who happen to be members of Parliament in the Republic of Serbia, the question may well arise, when you are in contact with your legal advisers, is it just a matter of discussing your case or is it a matter of discussing political issues; and if that is the case, you are having dealings with them on other matters other than your case, and this is what the issue hinges on. I assume that the Registrar wanted to check this out. It would be inconceivable, and you will be the first to understand this, I'm sure, for this Tribunal to fund a political activity. This would be paradoxical and certainly not in line with the Tribunal's mandate and not in line with the Registry's duties either. Therefore, the Registry has turned to these advisers and asked them whether they were solely involved in your case and not with any political matters. You know as well as we do that a lot has happened on the political scene over the last few months, so this is what this issue is all about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My telephone contacts with my legal advisers have been reduced to the use of a single telephone number, the telephone number of Slavko Jerkovic, as opposed to Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, who also defended himself and who had an office with a telephone at his disposal, and he could literally call whoever he wanted from that telephone, whoever he wanted; a potential witness, eyewitness, whoever, and so on and so forth. I am in a situation that I can only call Slavko Jerkovic. When I call Slavko Jerkovic, usually the conversations are attended by the other legal advisers, the case manager and the members of the professional team for preparing my Defence. Then the investigators are there and some other lawyers who do not have the rank of legal advisers but who do carry out very important work for me. I've been in detention for almost six years now, and I do have to have extended arms in Belgrade through which I'm going to carry out the work of preparing my Defence and cross-examining Prosecution witnesses. Also, I have to deal with administrative matters that are being imposed on me all the time. My conversations with legal advisers are confidential, in principle, and they have to remain confidential. The Registrar says, "You spoke before I did," and -- but that was the third problem that I wished to raise within the context of the first issue. The Registrar says that he has reason to believe that I perhaps made it possible to have the privileged telephone line abused. The Registrar has reason to believe that I may have made possible, et cetera. Just look at the formulation itself. That is self-revealing. On the basis of what is the Registrar saying that? Was he eavesdropping on my conversations? I don't think he's allowed to have intercepts, although I believe that all my conversations have been listened into. I'm deeply convinced of that. But from a legal point of view, no one is allowed to listen in. So I carry out these conversations. Perhaps sometimes a word or two is exchanged about the weather or whatever, so it's not that we only discuss my case. Who can establish that? No one. However, there is this new development. The former head of the team for my Defence, Tomislav Nikolic, who has been recruited in the meantime by some Western intelligence agencies so that he break up the Serbian Radical Party, and this time coincidence is no coincidence, the fact that the OTP asked for counsel to be imposed on me here, so now he is making statements to the effect that I made some political suggestions through that telephone. That's what he's been saying. Now, whether that's true or not, that is hard to establish. But as a rule, a man like that, who loses every moral criterion whatever, his word should not be taken for anything; especially the Registry should not be guided by his statements in the Serbian media. If the OTP has the reason for such suspicions, the OTP can call him as a witness. They can take a statement from him, they can bring him into the courtroom, and let that cooperation be manifested to a maximum here, then. For as long as this is -- this kind of cautious doubt, the Registry has no reason to do anything. You can deny me that telephone line. You can deny me legal advisers as well, members of the Defence team too. I will continue to defend myself even in that case literally on my own. However, do not forget, you are the ones who are in charge of the fairness of the trial. What is more important for you, as the Trial Chamber; to truly show to the public that this is a fair trial or to intervene with regard to some minor abuses like I asked about the weather in Belgrade or perhaps I said something else in passing? Is there a single telephone conversation between a lawyer and a client on this confidential line without something else being said in passing? Is that possible at all? Is it possible for them not to ask each other how they're doing, about the state of their health and so on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, things are very clear, as far as we Judges are concerned. You have a telephone line connecting you to Mr. Jerkovic. It's a confidential line, a protected line, and no one should listen in on conversations on that telephone line, because your adviser is in Belgrade. But if he was sitting next to you, if he was talking to you, no one would be allowed to listen in on your conversations. Therefore, we Judges believe that all conversations you have with Mr. Jerkovic are protected conversations, are secret conversations, and that no one except for you and your advisers should be aware of the contents of these conversations. This is a principle that no one can challenge. I'm listening to you, and I find out things that I was not aware of. Apparently, Mr. Nikolic, who was your main adviser at some point, because you told me during your pre-trial conference that he was in charge of your Defence, so apparently he said in the media that when he was on the phone with you, you would give him political instructions. That's it. I suppose based on that, informed of that, the Registrar had some concerns. You are responding. You are telling that Mr. Nikolic is no longer on your team. He can say things that are contrary to your interests and that what he says should not be taken into account. This is, therefore, a problem that may have existed in the past or may still exist, but in any case, the conversations you have with your advisers are secret conversations. I'm not entitled to find out the content of these conversations, and it's up to you and to your associates to deal only with your case during these conversations. I have no idea what Mr. Nikolic has said, but I suppose that what he said prompted the Registrar to raise a number of issues. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will be frank. I am embarrassed. I feel ashamed, truly ashamed, that Tomislav Nikolic had my unlimited trust for years. The extent of that trust and the confidence I had in him was such that I enabled him to be the main head of the team for my Defence, but that's my personal matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I believe that we should talk to -- stop talking about Mr. Nikolic, because Mr. Nikolic is no longer a member of your Defence team. So in this court, no mention should be made of Mr. Nikolic anymore.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that it's over with him in every respect. I will not talk about him any longer, but I also think the Registry cannot bring him up. They cannot bring up what Tomislav Nikolic says to the press. We don't care about that. His personal failure, his personal collapse, is of no interest to us. This is why I asked that these three problems, which come under the first issue, I ask you, the Trial Chamber, to prevent the Registry in any attempt of theirs to prevent me from cooperating with my legal advisers in the future. The minimum of cooperation that I had until now should be left intact. I don't know how the Defence case will be conducted unless your decision on funding Defence case is implemented. As I have said previously, I will not be raising that issue again, and I have gone against my word, and it was wrong of me, and I will not be bringing it up again. But let me tell you, it would be impermissible to prevent you from -- prevent me from communicating with my legal advisers and preventing them from visiting me, because who will assist me if not them? I trust only them, and I will not trust anyone else. That was the first issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you've just said something that caught my attention, even though it might not have raised other people's attention. You said that we would issue a decision about the funding of your Defence, but the decision we are going to issue in due course about the motion of the Prosecution is not directly related to the funding of your Defence. The financing of your legal advisers is a matter that has been resolved. The Trial Chamber held that your legal advisers are entitled to remuneration, as anyone doing any kind of work, and the Registrar in that respect requested a number of data and, among other things, asked you to tell us who, amongst these three, was the one who was an attorney-at-law. Mr. Jerkovic fitted the profile perfectly, but for mysterious reasons, which I completely fail to understand, for mysterious reasons you did not respond to the request. And as a result, the issue is still pending. The Registrar is still paying for the travel expenses of your advisers, but they were not actually entitled to any pay, although they are working. We may be able to find a solution to this issue. The easiest would be for you to respond to the request made to you by the Registrar at the time. You only had to tell him who, amongst these three men, is an attorney-at-law, has the status of a lawyer. Then the Registrar would move on to the following step. But you failed to respond to this request, and as a result the whole matter is on hold. You stated on your own that our decision blocks the funding of your team, but, no, it's not the case at all. The Trial Chamber has no say in the matter. A decision was issued. According to this decision, you are entitled to have associates, and these associates are entitled to be paid. That's all. We have no say in the matter whatsoever. The proper decisions have been issued. The problem now that needs to be resolved is between you and the Registrar; and the Registrar is simply waiting for you to tell him who is going to be in charge amongst these three men, who is going to be the attorney-at-law. And I always said Mr. Jerkovic fit the profile perfectly, but you did not respond to the Registrar. Here we are, Mr. Seselj. This is a minor matter, of course, but I wanted to make things very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that's exactly what I have done. I told to the Registry that I agree for Slavko Jerkovic to be in charge of the Defence funding, and I think I have stated that in the courtroom. You can find it in the transcript. I have stated that several months ago. So as far as Slavko Jerkovic is concerned, that matter is over. I don't know what else am I supposed to do, other than stand on my head, to convince the Registry that I have said that. Everything I utter here for the transcript is just as important as any written submission. At least that's how it is in the legal system where I come from. Everything that is uttered in the courtroom is equal to any written submissions given to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note of what you've just said, and I'm going to check it out, because if you have indeed told the Registrar that Slavko Jerkovic was to be in charge of your team, in that respect things should be moving ahead. But to be quite frank, I thought that we were still in this situation where no decision had been made because you had not responded to the Registrar's -- to the Registrar's request. But you've just said that you have done so, so we will check this. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the problem here is somewhat more complex. The Registry evades ruling on financing. That decision should detail what finances are available for pre-trial proceedings, for OTP case and for Defence case. The Registry is evading on that. Their interpretation was that the funding needs to start only once the trial begins, as though the pre-trial proceedings do not exist. The last time we spoke to (redacted), we argued about that. He came to the Detention Unit to speak to me. So there is no goodwill there. And then they ask all kinds of information from me, impossible things. They buried me with letters requiring things that are not possible, and this is why I did not respond to that. Now I would like to turn to the second important issue that I wanted to raise today. You gave me a deadline -- or, rather, you extended the deadline for my submission responding to the OTP request to impose a counsel on me. You extended that deadline by a month. My legal advisers drafted this reply. They will bring it with them and I will see it on Thursday -- or, rather, I will file it on Thursday, that is to say, one day before the deadline expires. However, during the last status conference, even though that wasn't its official name, but by nature that's what it was, a status conference which was held on the 26th of August, I drew your attention to the fact that the OTP motion was not delivered to me in its entirety. Then you ruled requiring the Prosecution to put back some redacted information into the version that was disclosed to me. To this day, I still am not familiar with over 50 per cent of the OTP motions, so I'm replying to you on Thursday while still in the dark. I can only assume what may be in that motion, because some paragraphs are redacted, more than 50 per cent of them redacted. Last time I referred to this as the Kafka-like procedure trial. I'm supposed to reply to something that I am not familiar with, so how can that reply be valid? Of course, I will reply in a certain manner, but that is not a manner that would be tolerated or upheld in a serious legal system. My fundamental right, right to defence, is being attacked here. Somebody is trying to deny my right to Defence by hiding from me the arguments as to why they're trying to deny me that right. You are familiar with these arguments because you received the motion in its entirety. The Prosecution is aware of these arguments. I'm the only one who's not, and I'm the one who has to reply to the Prosecution. I don't think that this would be allowed in the legal systems where you come from, Your Honours: The Italian, French or Danish system. I don't think so. In the 20th or the 21st century, a trial could not be held under these circumstances. This is something unbelievable. This is a model showing globalistic totalitarian judiciary. This exceeds both Hitler and Stalin. Hitler's and Stalin's judiciary were minor things compared to what is going on here, and once again I tell you this is impermissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I have to respond, I have to respond. If you say something and if the Judges do not respond, then they seem to be accepting that what you are saying is true. I must tell you, quite frankly, that I myself was very surprised, as you were, when I found out that in civil law countries, the adversarial rule is sacred. Here in this Tribunal, there are confidential and ex parte filings, of which the opposite party is not aware. I must say that when I found out about such procedures, I was astounded, so I looked into the matter further to try and find out why things were organised that way sometimes. And you have an answer in the Rules, Rules 75, regarding the protection of witnesses and victims, because in some cases to protect victims and witnesses, the accused may not, at the beginning, be notified of the identity of some witnesses or some victims, and in some cases it may only be notified of their identity 30 days before the witness comes to testify, or, in some cases, the day the witness comes to testify. It is a practice that is applied in this Tribunal. And beyond the victims and the witnesses, you have to also take into account Rule 70 related to documents provided by states. That's the way things work at this Tribunal. When the motion to impose counsel on you was filed, portions of this motion had been redacted. The Trial Chamber looked into the matter, on my own initiative, because the concept of the adversarial system is at the forefront of my mind, so that's why we asked the Prosecution to provide you with some of the information. But part of the information was not disclosed to you pursuant to Rule 75. Why? Well, because if this information was disclosed to you, this could cause a risk to these witnesses. Whether this risk is subjective or objective, well, now is not the time to deal with this. But the Trial Chamber looked into the matter extremely thoroughly for you not to be harmed in any way. And in the respond you are going to file, and you just said that you will be filing it Thursday; of course, you will not be able to respond to 50 per cent of this motion, but the response you will give on the other part of the motion will allow us to rule whilst being duly informed. If we had believed that your interest was prejudiced because you were not made aware of such-and-such information, we would have made sure that this information was provided to you. So you have to be convinced of one thing. You will not be prejudiced in any way on the substance of the matter because of the redactions that remain in the motion. Please wait for our decision, our ruling. Once the ruling has been handed down, you will be entitled, as the Prosecutor will be, will be entitled to appeal the ruling. So I've just explained to you why some information was not disclosed to you. It's a practice common in this Tribunal, but in your country or in my country, things do not happen that way. But things happen that way in this Tribunal. That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, during this trial against me, the Prosecution raised a sub-trial, a trial on the side. In relation to this sub-trial, minor trial, the purpose of which is to deny me the right to represent myself, or impose counsel on me, which is an identical thing, so in that sub-trial the same procedure needs to be upheld as in the rest of the trial. In this sub-trial, the procedural rules cannot be opposite of what they are in the other trial. You said so yourself. The responsibility to protect witnesses, victims and so on, but only within a certain period of time, not in absolute terms, because at some point I need to learn of the names of all witnesses, the content of all their statements and so on. This is why. At some point I also need to learn of the entire content of this motion of the Prosecution. When is that going to happen? I can only hope now that your ruling will be correct and that it would deny the motion of the Prosecution, in which case my basic interest would be protected, but it seems that even in that case I will never learn what arguments they deployed against me. Can anything in this trial, a single piece of paper, a single motion filed, remain secret to me? That's my essential question. I believe that it may not be. No matter what the nature of this trial is, I believe that until the end of the trial, all information disclosed in this trial needs to be made available to me. If some danger stems from the fact that information is disclosed to me, then the OTP has resources to eliminate that danger in their true-and-tested ways, but to deny me forever essential information, you know, perhaps there is something here that the Prosecution is right about, and then you need to make me aware of that so that I would learn it, so I would learn my lesson for the future. Imagine, you are trying me, you are putting me on trial, and this is an indictment, because this is a small-scale indictment in this sub-trial, and imagine the situation where you try me on the basis of an indictment, half of which I'm aware of and half of which I'm not; and that I'm denied the right to learn of one half of the indictment with the same arguments as were used in this motion. So what kind of argument would that be? That is the essence of what I'm speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me respond on this point. We have an indictment, and the Trial Chamber will rule based on this indictment and not on any imaginary indictment. Secondly, with respect to protected witnesses, of course in due course you will receive their full statements, because these witnesses will come to testify, and if for some reason, some of these witnesses do not show up, and if the Trial Chamber decides to admit their statements under Rule 92 ter/quater, these statements will be admitted and you will be able to read them. In due course, all these documents will be admitted and the Trial Chamber will rule strictly on the basis of admitted documents. It's not possible for the judgement to be based on documents that are not admitted, because if that was the case, yes, we could be talking about a Kafkaesque trial. Yes, of course, you have not received the statements of some witnesses. I agree. But, you see, I'm not afraid to speak my mind. What should have been done -- it's too late now. What should have been done is the following: When you have an indictment confirmed by Judges, this indictment should be accompanied by all documents, and I stressed "all documents," supporting the confirmation of the indictment so as to avoid any kind of ambiguity, because what's the situation? We have an indictment confirmed on the basis of a number of documents, but no one knows whether the supporting documents will be tendered during the proceedings or not, and this is a procedural problem that was never resolved in this Tribunal. What you are raising now would be irrelevant and would not happen if the Judges who drafted the Rules had stated that all supporting documents have to be provided with the indictment, but that's not the way things happened and that's why now you can tell us that you're rather taken aback by the types of documents disclosed to you. You are wondering whether some of these documents will never be disclosed to you. But I don't think so, because when the witnesses come to testify, their statements will be admitted. But, of course, some witnesses listed may not testify, and their statements may then be admitted. But, and I'd like to thank you for raising this issue, if a protected witness, whose identity is supposed to be disclosed 30 days before his testimony, if that witness does not come to testify, is the Prosecution forced to disclose his testimony to you? That's a matter I'm going to address with my fellow Judges. We'll be thinking about this, because I don't think that there is a clear answer to this issue. Here, again, we are dealing with a matter that is extremely interesting, but notwithstanding all these issues, all these problems, when a judgement is handed down, this judgement is based solely and refers solely to admitted documents. The judgement refers to the transcript of the witnesses' testimony at trial. It also refers to written statements admitted under Rules 92 ter, bis, or quater. That's all I can tell you at this stage. I can't go any further. Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next issue that I wish to raise is actually my repeated request, repeated on several occasions, for reconsidering one of your decisions. I included now new arguments, so I hope that it is not misplaced to raise this issue again. This has to do with your decision on accepting witnesses under Rule 92 ter. One of the reasons this rule was introduced into the Rules of Procedure, even though it should not pertain to me because my indictment was written prior to this Rule being introduced, so one of the reasons for its existence is the economy of time. I've been saving time for over six years now here, and I think that I have saved so much that I think that it is pointless for somebody else to speak to me about saving time. We have lost one month just now due to frivolity of the Prosecution, sheer frivolity. During this month, we could have completed perhaps four, five, perhaps even six witnesses, which means the trial has been extended at least a month. Now that we have lost this month, I now ask you to reconsider your decision concerning witnesses under 92 ter and perhaps lose another month, but at least not have any more witnesses under Rule 92 ter but, rather, all viva voce witnesses. There are multiple problems here. For example, several days ago I received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, for it to be quite clear, I would like to say that we have a number of requests for review coming from you. You may submit these requests if you have new facts, not if you have arguments. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is a new fact that we've lost a month on account of the arrogance of the OTP. On the one hand, we are saving time in violating my procedural rights, because there is retroactive imposition of the Rule that did not exist at the time my indictment was issued. And, on the other hand, out of sheer arrogance on the part of the OTP, time is being squandered. If that is not an argument then nothing doing. But anyway, I'm just going to tell you one more thing so that you have that in mind as well. I got yet another statement of Witness VS-131 [as interpreted]. The witness statement is from the 9th of September, I think. He testified earlier on in other cases and so on, and I read that statement. He refers to me in a single sentence, saying that he had heard that in November 1991, I was in Vukovar; nothing else. Now, when you look at that statement, you may easily think that this statement may be a 92 ter statement. However, that statement -- that witness had such an important position that there is no way that he can just march through this courtroom under 92 ter. Look at the high office he held. And what office did I hold at that time? This enormous discrepancy has to be my new argument as to why that kind of thing should not be allowed to happen. If you are not in a mood to discuss this question at all, then perhaps we can deal with it that way too. I'm not opposed to that either. It was for me to try once again. And the fourth issue, and I'm going to conclude on that note, I inform you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. I believe there must be a mistake on the transcript. It's not Witness 131, it should be Witness VS-1131.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness 1131, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You did well to address this issue. In light of the Prosecution's schedule, theoretically this witness is due to come. I shall not give his name, since he has been granted protective measures. But normally speaking, he's due to come at the beginning of November. We shall look into this case again, but a decision has been handed down and it has been stated that this is a 92 ter witness. There's no reason to overturn this. We have noted what you are saying and what the Prosecution is saying, and we shall review the issue. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You decided to agree to the Prosecution motion to include Vesna Bosanac on the witness list. I did not oppose that at all, but I never received a decision from you to the effect that Vesna Bosanac would be testifying under Rule 92 ter. When the Prosecutor submitted that request, I opposed it here in court. Maybe you received that, but I did not. And here in the schedule that was provided to me by the OTP, it says that Vesna Bosanac would testify as a 92 ter witness. That is the latest schedule. I think that that is absolutely impermissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My colleague has just told me that this is a mistake. Normally speaking, she should testify viva voce. Furthermore, no decision has been taken as regarding her testimony under 92 ter, so at first sight, when the Judges deliberated on this matter, I believe this witness is going to come to testify as a viva voce witness. I don't know why the Prosecution has stated that this is a 92 ter witness. We shall look into this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Imagine, Mr. President, when I received this on Friday evening and when I saw that Vesna Bosanac is testifying under 92 ter. Can you imagine what kind of stress I suffered and how long I couldn't sleep that night because of this minor alleged error on the part of the Prosecution? The fifth question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I said there was a mistake. I don't know. Mr. Mundis or Mrs. Dahl, as far as this witness is concerned, can you shed some light on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, and everyone in and around the courtroom. The Prosecution is always endeavouring to reduce the amount of time we spend on witness testimony. It's anticipated that we will be filing a 92 ter request with respect to this witness. We have not done so as of today. If we decide to do that, we will certainly do it with enough notice under the Trial Chamber's guidelines in order to allow the accused to respond. In putting together the calendars, what we simply try to do is try to note as much information as possible so the schedule, on its face, looks realistic. You will note that this witness is down for two days, that was done in the event that the 92 ter request, if we make one, that request would be denied, there would be adequate time on the calender for the witness to complete her testimony. That's why she's down both under 92 ter but also holding two dates on the calender so we've got both bases covered. In the event we make the application, there will certainly be adequate time for the accused to respond to our motion, and it's at this point certainly premature to be discussing this at any great length, because we have not filed an application, nor has a decision been taken that we will file an application. Let's, with all due respect, move on in the interests of economy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So no decision -- no submissions have been filed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After all, this is an official document of the OTP that I received, so I have been misled. I believe that you share my view on that matter. And the fifth question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. This is an official document, since it stems from the OTP, but you know as well as I do that this is a preparatory document, preparing for hearings, which holds an approximate value, since in certain cases some witnesses don't come, some witnesses' names are taken off the list. This is a working instrument, a working paper. It does not provide a 100 per cent guarantee. It doesn't mean that one is going to stick to the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last thing that I wanted to say to you today, that is to say, the fifth question that I wanted to deal with: I inform you now orally that on Friday I'm going to submit a request in writing that you give me certification to appeal your decision of the 11th of September that was submitted to me on the 19th of September, on the basis of the oral request made by the OTP to admit three statements of Witness Nebojsa Stojanovic. I believe that even as far as this Tribunal is concerned, and I have the most negative possible opinion of it, that what happened was unprecedented, along with a witness who testified viva voce, and the Prosecution is not happy with his testimony. They want to admit into evidence his alleged statements that the Prosecutors themselves wrote for him, and investigators too. You made a decision that these written statements can be admitted into evidence in order to challenge the authenticity of Mr. Stojanovic's statement and also the veracity of the content. You said at one point that as for the probative value of these statements, you are yet to assess it. I think that this is something that is absolutely untenable, and if it remains this way, it brings into question the regularity of the entire trial. Well, you're the ones who gave me guarantees here. As far as I can remember, it was Judge Harhoff explicitly, only recently, that when the judgement is being made, only what was stated in court can be taken into account, not what the Prosecution prepared for a witness who they blackmailed, exerted pressure against, promised him, whatever. It's all the same to me. But the witness said that that was not true here in court before all of us. If you think that you have proof to the effect that the witness did not give truthful testimony in the courtroom, then proceedings can be initiated against him on account of perjury, but you don't have such proof. Nevertheless, you want to admit into evidence his alleged statements that were written by the Prosecutors themselves. And in the words of that witness, when signing these statements, he did not even read them. I really find it unbelievable that you made such a decision, so I am going to submit a request for you to allow me to appeal on Friday, and that is, I imagine, my legal deadline. My legal advisers are going to bring me the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall look into this again. This did not seem to me to be such a vital matter, and I didn't believe that this should be addressed. Of course, you are entitled to ask for a certification to appeal this. You have addressed all the topics you wish to. Mr. Prosecutor and Mrs. Dahl, are there any issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have three very brief issues to raise, and then I will turn to my co-counsel, Ms. Dahl, for an additional issue or two. First, though, let me -- the first point I simply wanted to make -- the first and second points I want to make relate to issues raised by Dr. Seselj earlier this morning. I think it's important, in the overall context of discussions concerning his legal advisers, to also put onto the record the fact that the legal advisers have also entered into and signed the code of conduct that governs the conduct of Defence counsel appearing before this international tribunal, and whether or not Dr. Seselj likes that fact, they are indeed subject to the code of conduct, having voluntarily signed that document in order to be accredited as his legal advisers or associates. So I do want to put that point on the record. The second point relates to comments made by Dr. Seselj this morning concerning the Prosecution motion to assign counsel and the fact, as he's put it, that 50 per cent of that document would remain ex parte as to him. And, again, simply to put onto the record, I would like to indicate that in our filing on the 28th of July, 2008, paragraph 137, the final paragraph of that pleading, subparagraph (b), the Prosecution specifically asked for the immediate assignment of independent counsel to make ex parte written submissions to the Trial Chamber with respect to the ex parte material; and so I to want to put on the record the fact that we did propose, as part of our motion, that independent counsel be assigned to look at those parts of our pleadings which are ex parte as to the accused, and we had requested that again, with all due respect, immediate assignment on the 28th of July. So I do want to put that point on the record. The final point that I had this morning before turning to my colleague Ms. Dahl concerns the Trial Chamber's decision of 18 September 2008, and I don't want to dwell on this at any great length of time, but I would suggest perhaps it might be helpful to the parties for some clarification. And that might not need to be done today. But in light of that decision, the Prosecution, at least, has some concern about the effective decision of that document as it relates to our ability to show exhibits to subsequent witnesses, the handling of exhibits in open court, the handling of exhibits when we're proofing witnesses, et cetera; because it is unclear to us, if that decision relates only to the Registry in terms of dissemination of exhibits or if that means, for example, if we were in open session and we want to show a previously admitted exhibit, would that run afoul of the decision by making those exhibits known to the public, when in fact, at least based on our reading of the decision, the Registry would not be allowed to distribute those exhibits to the public. So we do have some questions and some possible concerns about that, and it might be helpful in the near future to either discuss this or perhaps if the Trial Chamber could issue some clarification with respect to that decision, because to be as transparent and frank as possible, it does cause a little bit of confusion at least for us here in the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Two points, Mr. Mundis. You are quite right in saying that in your motion, you had asked an independent counsel to be appointed. This counsel would have at his disposal all the documents, and I emphasise this, all the documents. This definitely has to be on the transcript. Mr. Seselj, in the Prosecutor's filings, no secret was made, because an independent counsel could have had access to these documents. It so happens that the Trial Chamber decided to the contrary and decided that there was no need to have such an independent counsel. Therefore, these documents have not been disclosed. Mr. Mundis is quite right to remind us of this. The second point, Mr. Seselj, the decision handed down on the 18th of September, 2008, I believe you referred to a decision taken by the Trial Chamber regarding the request filed by a country to access documents. The Trial Chamber, in its decision, was extremely clear and stipulated that during the proceedings, no document would be disclosed to anyone, and it is only at the end of the trial that the document will be communicated to third parties that have nothing to do with this trial: Individuals, private individuals, or states. And the decision did not stipulate and never addressed the issue, i.e., that as far as documents which are tendered by the Prosecution, that these documents be not addressed in public. When a document is not under seal and has no reason to be kept secret from anyone, this can be discussed, placed on the ELMO, and seen by all and everyone. So the decision taken on the 18th of September only relates to those documents and exhibits by states or individuals who are outside; in other words, for those parties who wish to establish some form of material communication. But to give a document to someone who wishes to see these documents, well, one can only grant this request at the end of the trial. Nothing prevents the Prosecution or the parties from showing a document in public, either on the ELMO or on the screen if it's in the e-court system, in such a way that the document or the transcript can be seen by the public. Now, if a third party wishes to access these documents, he can just record what is displayed on the screen. I don't know if I have answered your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You have, Mr. President, and the last point is the one that, to a certain extent, causes us some concern. Speaking on behalf of the Prosecution, and I believe probably also Mr. Seselj would share this view, knowing the position he's taken in the past, this would seem to be a slight infringement upon the ability of the public to have access to public exhibits in this trial. And as Your Honour has just indicated, anyone who has the technology or the wherewithal to simply record the proceedings or get a screen shot of any document shown on the ELMO would, in fact, have a copy of these materials, but someone who didn't have that technological capability, but simply made a telephone call to the Registry and said, "I would like this exhibit," would not be in a position to get the document or documents in question. And so we do have some concerns about the ability of the public to contact the press office and request an exhibit that is not under seal, that is, a public exhibit; for the simple reason that if they're shown on the television and they're broadcast to the public, they are, in fact, public documents, and we fail to see -- with the greatest of respect, we fail to see the difference between someone who can record it and get a screen shot and print the document at home on their computer and someone who doesn't have that ability, who would call the press office and say, "I'd like a copy of this exhibit," and which pursuant to the decision, they would not be able to do that. And so we do have some concerns as to how this decision impacts upon a certain segment and perhaps a large segment of the population who might not have the technological capabilities at hand in order to save and download any of these materials that they might otherwise want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I've been here now for five years, and it's the first time, as far as I know, that somebody has asked to see a document; it's the first time ever, so this is an exceptional circumstance. Someone, and in this particular case it's a state, has asked to see a document. Maybe some people in the past have already asked to see a number of documents. Since this is a public trial, people can listen to the proceedings, they can watch, they can print out material, they can make copies if they have enough resources to do so, make copies of documents. Let's take the case of someone who is in a country in Africa, who would like to dispose of such-and-such a document. This person would say that he does not have a television set and doesn't have a printer. And given where this person is living, he wishes to see the document. This means that he knows that the document exists already. Now, according to the reasoning of the Trial Chamber, which is spelled out in its decision, we have stated that these documents would be assessed by the Trial Chamber at the end of the trial. When the Prosecutor introduces a document, the Prosecutor then asks for the document to be tendered. If the document is then relevant, it does have a certain probative value, which can be higher, lower, or no probative value at all, but this document in itself will or might be challenged by the Defence during cross-examination or when the Defence will call its own witnesses and present its own documents. Then the document that has been admitted will be confronted to the other documents. So a document which we know will have a certain probative value in a particular case may all of a sudden have no probative value at all. So the Trial Chamber does run this risk. Let's assume that somebody would like to see a document and let's say the Trial Chamber grants a request and says, "You may see this document." When the document has not been assessed at all, since the proceedings are still ongoing, and the probative value of the document will only be assessed right at the end. So if we send out a document without having assessed it, we are running a risk because the person who is somewhere in a faraway country will not have these other documents that could challenge the first document, so he could be misled. This is why the Trial Chamber has decided to take this position, and the response will be provided at the end of the trial. If there are other people who wish to see some of the documents, we shall also respond in the same way, and we shall always say that this can only be done at the end of the trial. However, a document which is placed on the ELMO and is discussed at trial, as part of the adversarial system, if someone would like to make a copy, then he's free to do so, he or she is free to do so. That's got nothing to do with the Trial Chamber. The document itself will only be assessed at the end of the trial. A document cannot be disclosed to anyone whilst the trial is still ongoing. What tells you that this document is a true document? It could be a forged document. This document could be challenged during cross-examination by the Defence and by Defence witnesses. At first sight, the document may seem important, but when compared with a whole series of other documents, maybe it's not that important at all. This is why we have taken this decision. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, I find this debate to be very interesting, because I haven't got the slightest idea as to what all this is about. I never received this request, and I never received your decision in this regard; so could you please briefly inform me as to what this is all about, what state, what document? I believe that then I will find the debate even more interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but we are dealing with this, we are entering a discussion, but you have not seen the discussion -- the decision. On the 18th of September, 2008, we issued a ruling about the recording of a conversation between Karadzic and Milosevic. We wanted to find out what was in that recording and in all the other recordings. The Trial Chamber issued a ruling stating that this would be disclosed only at the end of the trial. Please wait for the translation of this decision in your own language. You are one of the addressees of this decision, of course, and once you have received the translation, you'll have all the data. But this is a premature discussion maybe, Mr. Mundis, because Mr. Seselj has not been made aware of the contents of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, and we can return to it perhaps in the next day or so. I understand or my understanding was the document had been translated and was to be provided to Dr. Seselj either yesterday or earlier this morning. Let me, though -- I know it's time for the recess. Let me just make two very quick observations, if I might. The first one relates to the statement by the Presiding Judge that this was the first time the Trial Chamber was aware of a request for access to exhibits in this trial. My sense is, if the press office were to be asked to provide such information, that there are a number of regular and recurring such requests. Based on the trials I've been involved in, I personally get numerous requests from the public and the media for access to material that has been openly admitted in trial, so I think that this is an extremely common thing where members of the public contact the press office for copies of exhibits, photographs, videos, other material that's openly played in court, and perhaps there was a translation or an interpretation error; but I do believe that this is an extremely common thing by members of the public. I do appreciate the difference between the Trial Chamber's use of all the evidence and waiting until all the evidence is admitted at the end and weighing up, and that processing of determining the relevance, probative value, et cetera, of each and every exhibit; but our concern is that notwithstanding that process, which is an ongoing one and which is only completed at the end of the evidentiary phase of the trial in toto, our concern remains that an individual member of the public who requested a particular document, photograph, a videotape, other exhibit that was openly admitted, would be denied access to that on the grounds that the dossier, if you will, is not complete because the evidentiary process is ongoing; and that remains our concern with respect to the completely open and public nature of these proceedings and trying to keep the proceedings as open to the public as possible. Obviously, documents or exhibits submitted under seal is a completely different story. The need to protect witnesses is a completely different story. But to be quite frank, we don't see why exhibits that are public should not be made available to the public by way of the press office when a request comes in. And I understand the process that the Chamber's going to use in weighing up all of the evidence, but our concern relates more to the public access and public nature of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to break now, unless Ms. Dahl only wants to take the floor for a few minutes. We have two options. Either you have very little to say and then we adjourn, or we have a break and you can take the floor after the break. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I regret to tell the Chamber I have a bit more than a little to say, and I think it would be prudent for me to begin after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in session. Ms. Dahl, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to request that we move into private session, because I have a matter to discuss concerning protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Prosecutor, before we adjourn, I wanted to draw your attention upon the following: According to the calculations made by the legal officer, together with the Registrar, you have had 72 hours and 37 minutes so far. The Trial Chamber granted you 120 hours, which means that you have 47 hours and 23 minutes left. Initially, you had planned to hear 100 witnesses. So far, we have heard 38 witnesses. As far as the remaining witnesses are concerned, well, these will have to be heard within these 47 hours and 23 minutes. This is what I wanted to share with you so that you can think about it and give us a new witness list, an updated witness list, notwithstanding all the pending motions. So that things are clear, I would like to thank you for the chart you gave us for the upcoming months, September and to November. You have planned to call a number of witnesses - that's fine - which means that you will undoubtedly wish to call witnesses in December and January. But we will wait until the time comes. Now, having addressed all the issues today, the Trial Chamber will deliberate, and I would like to say that after our deliberations, through our legal officer, who will send you an e-mail, we will tell you what has been decided as regards the protective measures for tomorrow. It seems to me that the Prosecutor needs three hours for its examination-in-chief. Is that right, Ms. Dahl? For tomorrow's witness, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm planning my examination hopefully to conclude within two hours, because I would like to conclude the witness's testimony this week. Sometimes my estimates are optimistic, but we're not sitting on Tuesday, I understand, because of the holiday, so the witness would be here for quite a bit of time. And I believe that Mr. Mundis would like to address the Chamber on the witness issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we reckon on two hours, and Mr. Seselj will also have two hours for his cross-examination. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With respect to the issue of the amount of time that remains for the Prosecution case, we will provide an updated witness list for the benefit of the Chamber and Dr. Seselj, but I do want to point out a couple of issues with respect to that. As the Chamber is very fully aware, a number of witnesses who were on the Prosecution list, for lack of a better term, are being contested by the accused, who claims that they are Defence witnesses and should not be Prosecution witnesses. Obviously, that's an issue that the Trial Chamber will have to reconcile at some point in time. Let me say this, however: Leaving aside those witnesses whom the Prosecution believes are extremely important witnesses for the Chamber and must be heard, regardless of whether they're heard during the Prosecution case or if they're called by the Trial Chamber, our view, as I've indicated previously, is that they must be heard before the 98 bis phase. Leaving those witnesses aside, however, in other words, if I were to take those witnesses off of the list in terms of planning, the remaining Prosecution witnesses on the Prosecution list we would have no problem finishing in the 47 hours and 23 minutes left available to us and would take the Prosecution case into late January/early February based on the rate at which we've been progressing thus far in this trial. But I do want to alert the Trial Chamber to the fact that it has always been our position that the witnesses whose name appear on the Prosecution list must be heard by the Trial Chamber and must be heard prior to the 98 bis phase. So I will provide an updated witness list, if you will. It will contain the names of a number of witnesses for whom Dr. Seselj has said will be Defence witnesses. It will contain those names of witnesses for whom Mr. Seselj has recently filed a motion concerning their status and the steps that he has asked the Trial Chamber to take with respect to those witnesses. So I will flag that up right up front, and perhaps what I will do is provide, for purposes of planning and so the Chamber can clearly see the time estimates, I will provide two lists; a complete list with all of the witnesses and a second list that has the names of only those witnesses -- or taking off of the first list those witnesses for whom Dr. Seselj is adamant that they be Defence witnesses and Defence witnesses only, and that will be -- will permit the Chamber, at an easy glance, to see the time estimates with respect to both scenarios while the Chamber is deliberating on that matter with respect to the accused. But we will provide these lists. I hope to do that perhaps by the end of this week. But I do want to make clear that we will be providing and circulating two such lists, and I don't believe, leaving aside the witnesses that again, for lack of a better word, are being contested by the accused, putting those witnesses aside for the moment, we certainly would have no problem finishing the Prosecution case with the other witnesses. But, again, that's going to take us into early February at the rate we're currently progressing. And, again, our view is very forcefully that those witnesses must be heard before the Trial Chamber goes through the 98 bis process in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as the current rate is concerned, I can't do more than I'm currently doing. I am sitting in another trial, and I cannot hold hearings around the clock. If people wish to start at 5.00 in the morning, I'm perfectly willing to do so. It's not a problem for me. We can start off at 5.00 in the morning, but of course this will pose a number of logistics problems. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few objections to what Mr. Mundis said. First of all, I would like to refer to the information you provided about the time used by counsel for the Prosecution within the 120 hours granted to them. I object, because additional examinations or re-examinations have not been included in that time, also the playing of video and audio-recordings in court. I believe that all of that is part of the Prosecution case, and I think that all of that should be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj, to avoid you from getting lost in all of this. The question -- the Prosecution will raise its question in the time that has been allotted to it. When there have been requests for admissions of the videos, this is part of the Prosecution's case and the Prosecution's time. This is what I need to tell you. But the Registrar must check all this out. I'll give you the floor back again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I even made a mistake. I do not rule out that possibility. But I would like this to be checked out, because the Registry provided me specific information at the end of July, at my request, and I seem to remember that re-examination was not included in the time. However, if I'm making a mistake, I apologise in advance, but I still think I'm not making a mistake. It is not impossible, but I think I am not wrong. And I think that the time we had with this witness, who came with the intercepts of telephone conversations, was not included either. And then we listened to these intercepts and so on and so forth. However, if the Registry checks this, then I'm going to believe that information. If the Registrar corrects me, then I am sorry for having raised the issue in the first place. Secondly, which is far more important as far as I'm concerned, I expect the Prosecution to ask for an extension of time for the Prosecution case, and I tell you in advance that I'm going to oppose that vehemently. The Prosecution used up too much time irrationally, anyway, even in order to prove the crime base in those localities that have been excluded from the indictment, and in accordance with the ruling of the previous Trial Chamber, it was only a pattern of behaviour that was dealt with in that evidence. Also, there were other witnesses that were a mistake on their part, and they did not really prove anything, and that certainly did not support or could not support the indictment, but that is the Prosecutor's problem. As for these 18 witnesses that keep stating that they are Defence witnesses and assist me in my Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, then, there can be no motion. We will discuss this if there is a motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague is quite right, Mr. Seselj. For the time, the Prosecution has not asked to have any extra time, and I'm really quite clear to the Prosecution that as far as the remaining witnesses are concerned, these have to be part of those 47 hours that are still available. The Prosecution can file a request -- a motion, and in that case you are able to respond and the Trial Chamber will rule on this, and the Appeals Chamber can also rule on that. I think we all agree on this. For the time being, no motion has been filed with a view to extending the time of the Prosecution. The Prosecution might file such a motion. In that case, you can reply, and the Trial Chamber will rule on it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very sorry that I listened to Mr. Mundis so carefully, and I did not miss that implicitly Mr. Mundis stated what the expectations of the OTP were; that these 18 witnesses should be taken over by you as Chamber witnesses. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted). Whether you're going to deal with others that way remains to be seen. However, if you had taken that path, I have no reason to believe that you're now going to persist in this and that the other 18 are also going to be behind bars. However, that is no way to achieve what the Prosecution wants. You see, if the Prosecution has that kind of case where 18 persons do not want to be Prosecution witnesses at any cost, then they are powerless. Then these witnesses should be Defence witnesses, because obviously that is what these people want to be. Again, we are going to have a situation where all 18 of these witnesses will certainly deny the truthfulness and authenticity of these statements here in the courtroom, those that were written by the Prosecutor and that were represented here as witness statements. You saw the case of Nebojsa Stojanovic; not to go into motives why some things were signed earlier on and why they're now being denied, only those for whom the Prosecution provide residence in a Western country, money to run their own business, a job, to care for their families, they are the only ones who come here and confirm what is stated in their statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm sorry if I interrupt you, but this is something you have mentioned already. This is familiar to the Trial Chamber. You've told the Trial Chamber already. And you are quite right to mention this, and so is Mr. Mundis. The legal situation is as follows: There are 18 witnesses, and the Trial Chamber needs to take a stance on this. Rest assured the Trial Chamber will rule on the matter very quickly, so you will get an answer to this very quickly. Do you have any other issues you would like to address?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd just like to remind you that I submitted this in writing as well. I submitted a motion to you about a month ago including the statements of all of those witnesses. I hope that you are going to rule on that motion of mine as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Seselj. We shall meet again tomorrow for the hearing, which will start, as you know, at 8.30, since we are sitting in the morning. The Trial Chamber will withdraw and deliberate, as I have said, and we will get back to you as soon as possible; more specifically, regarding the upcoming witness. I wish you a pleasant afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of September 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.16 a.m.,
